items.title: Jimmy and Jeannie Cheatham interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 12, 1998
items.q: Papa Jo Jones was like a mentor you see and everything. I mean he raised me professionally and everything.

ctx.x: Like she said, one of the saddest things, like was when Papa Jo Jones was like a mentor you see and everything. I mean he raised me professionally and everything. And wherever we went after we left New York, and I was called to Bennington to teach and then Wisconsin and finally L.A. But the thing is is that he would show up at my first concert, wherever I held it. And nobody’d tell him.
He’d just be sitting there backstage there in the chair with his handkerchief.

items.title: Jimmy and Jeannie Cheatham interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 12, 1998
items.q: I said, “Jo Jones, you’re going to have to go out on the patio and smoke.” And so he went back to New York and we got calls all week long, “You threw Jo Jones out?” “You put Papa Jo out?” I said yes we did.

ctx.x: And I had just come back from California, not too long beforehand. And so that was kind of a habitual thing. After the gig was over and the pack up, and as Papa Jo Jones would say, “With our mutual armies we’ll move out smiling.”

But I was always hanging around because I liked the stories. See because he had more of an advantage in that he had a chance to grow up listening to people and talking to people like Jo Jones and Ben Webster—
